ic_se_note: Standard error uses 87 effective dates, not 261 calendar dates: a 63-day horizon sampled every 21 days means consecutive observations share most of their window.
pooled_vs_per_date_note: Pooled IC (-0.054) differs from the per-date mean (+0.008) by -0.062. That gap is market timing, not stock ranking: the score tended to be high in periods that turned out badly. Only the per-date figure measures stock selection.

stability.verdict: Sub-period ICs change sign (-0.010 to +0.034) but all sit close to zero. Consistent with there being no relationship at all, rather than a relationship that flips.

bucket_note: Read the cross-sectional table. The raw table pools dates, so a bucket populated mostly during one good quarter looks skilful when it is not.
verdict: Mean IC +0.008 +/- 0.014 (t=+0.57). INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ZERO. The score orders stocks about as well as alphabetical order would. This is a genuine null, not a negative -- the composite is not backwards, it is uninformative. Check the component table: a flat composite can still contain parts that work.
warnings: News is excluded: no free provider offers historical archives, so including it would be look-ahead bias.
Macro is excluded: FRED serves revised data, and the CPI print for a past month is not the number published at the time. Use ALFRED vintages before enabling it.
96 ticker(s) have no price history back to 2011-06-07 and contribute only from their listing date: ALLY, AMLX, AMPL, AMR, ANET, APPF, ARHS, ARX....
how_to_read: information_coefficient is the average per-date rank correlation between the score and what happened next: did the score order that morning's candidates correctly? Judge it against ic_std_error, not against zero. Then check stability -- an average that hides a sign flip between periods is a fitted regime, not an edge.

sample_adequacy.verdict: Wide enough to detect an effect down to about 0.009, which covers the range real equity signals occupy. A null result here is meaningful.

universe.name: screen
universe.survivorship_warning: Survivorship bias: universe chosen in 2026 from companies that still exist in 2026. Firms that failed, were acquired, or dropped out of the index are absent, which flatters returns. Read the information coefficient, not the return figures. A clean test needs historical index membership, which is not free.

multiple_testing.note: 6 ranking components tested at once. At the usual |t| > 2 bar the chance of at least one false positive somewhere in the table is roughly 26%, so the bar is raised accordingly.

attribution.diagnosis: Composite IC +0.008 and no individual component clears ±0.02. On this sample nothing measurable is happening in either direction. Before concluding the engine has no edge, widen the universe — ranking eight names per date cannot resolve an effect this size.

weight_fitting.guidance: Fitted weights score +0.043 versus +0.012 out of sample (+0.031). Suggested: valuation 82%, technical 14%, money_flow 4%. Treat this as a hypothesis, not a conclusion — re-run on a different universe and a different date range before changing WEIGHTS in decision.py.

event_study.verdict: None of the 7 testable hypotheses cleared |t| > 2.73. 8-K events do not predict abnormal returns on this sample. They remain useful as facts — an auditor resignation is worth reading about whether or not it is tradeable — but they should not enter a score.
event_study.confirmation_note: `awaiting_confirmation` holds hypotheses found by exploration in an earlier run. They are not evidence, and cannot become evidence on the sample that produced them. Check `is_confirmation` on each: false means this run is a restatement, not a test.
event_study.preregistration_note: 8 hypotheses were declared in code before any result was seen, and the correction is applied to all of them rather than to the survivors. Anything under `exploratory` was not declared and does not count as evidence.
